```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 04_variability_differences
title: >
  Comparing movie ratings
questions:
  - id: differences
    type: free-response
    checkLabel: Save response
    prompt: >
      How might you describe the differences among these sets of ratings? Don't worry
      about calculating any new statistics yet. Start with the ideas from the previous
      chapter and think about what they capture or leave out.
    explanation: >
      There's no single required description. If you noticed that the sets can
      resemble one another in some ways and look quite different in others, you've
      found the issue to keep hold of. We'll put it into more precise terms after the
      next question.

  - id: you_friend
    type: free-response
    checkLabel: Compare your answer
    prompt: >
      Suppose you're about to watch each movie and add your own review. What rating
      would you predict you'll give each one? Explain what in the existing ratings
      would make you more or less confident in those predictions.
    answer: >
      A reasonable prediction is 5 for each movie because all three have a mean and
      median of 5. But I would be most confident about *Fine, Actually*, where every
      rating so far is 5, and least confident about *The Polarizing Express*, where
      every rating is far from 5. *The Good, the Bad and the Okay* sits somewhere
      in between.
```
